paper.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
paper.central_claim: MemRL: a frozen LLM agent self-evolves without weight updates by storing Intent-Experience-Utility triplets and learning Q-values over memories from environment rewards, with two-phase retrieval (similarity recall, then Q-aware re-ranking), outperforming RAG/Self-RAG/Mem0/MemP on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld and Lifelong Agent Bench in both runtime-learning and transfer settings.

signatures.object: Episodic memory bank M={(intent z, LLM-summarised experience e, utility Q)} and the retrieval policy over it (frozen backbone LLM unchanged)
signatures.information: Query embedding, stored triplets, environment reward per attempt (ground-truth or execution verifier); HLE correctness labels in the loop
signatures.operation: Phase A recall: cosine > delta, top-k1; Phase B select top-k2 by (1-lambda)*z(sim)+lambda*z(Q); inject; act; EMA update Q of injected items with reward (alpha=0.3); summarise trajectory and append new triplet (Q_init=0)
signatures.output: Updated Q-values and a new triplet per attempt
signatures.conditions: Rewards in [-1,1]; stationarity assumption for the theorem; per-benchmark delta/k1/k2
signatures.selection_rule: No admission gate (all trajectories written); utility only re-ranks retrieval
signatures.persistence: Memory bank with Q-values, mutable and prunable in principle; no retirement implemented
signatures.later_use: Retrieved into prompts on later tasks (same epoch stream and later epochs; frozen for transfer tests)
signatures.claimed_effect: Table 1 avg Last/CSR 0.772/0.798 vs MemP 0.736/0.760, No Memory 0.631; Table 2 avg 0.794 vs MemP 0.766, No Memory 0.709
signatures.failure_boundary: Low task similarity degrades to reflection-like behaviour; reward-hacking sensitivity; unbounded memory growth; noisy credit when several memories are injected

signatures.information: Runtime: the same task set replayed for 10 epochs with labelled rewards; Transfer: frozen memory, held-out 30% split (OS/DB/BCB) or 140 ALFWorld valid_seen instances
signatures.operation: Report last-epoch SR and CSR; frozen-bank test
signatures.conditions: HLE has no transfer split; HLE prompt template may carry CORRECT/INCORRECT on the replayed question (E028)
signatures.failure_boundary: Runtime numbers are on the learning stream; HLE gain self-described as memorisation

gap.author_gap: Fine-tuning costs and forgets; memory/RAG agents retrieve by semantic similarity, so noisy but similar experiences are injected and runtime feedback does not separate high-value strategies from distractors.
gap.checked_gap: 'Similar is not useful' is a real, widely recognised retrieval limitation; the paper builds directly on the M-MDP formulation of Zhou et al. 2025a (retrieval as an MDP action), so the delta is non-parametric, EMA-based utility on stored items rather than the retrieval-as-decision framing itself. That prior is cited but not run as a baseline.
lineage: RAG/Self-RAG -> agentic memory (Reflexion, MemGPT, Mem0, MemP) -> value-aware episodic retrieval (Q-values; Zhou et al. 2025a M-MDP, NEC-style episodic control) -> MemRL
closest_adjacent: Zhou et al. 2025a learned retrieval (cited, not compared)
gap.residue: Credit assignment among co-injected memories, memory growth/consolidation, robustness to wrong rewards, behaviour at low task similarity (author-acknowledged).
gap.stakes: Quality of injected context and forgetting in long deployments.
gap.method_response: Q-values per stored experience updated from rewards and combined with similarity at retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: Does not address write-side admission, retirement, or poisoned feedback; comparison to learned-retriever neighbours is absent.
unresolved: Delta vs the cited learned-retrieval M-MDP baseline is not measured.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus confirms son55. Primary adapt_via_conditioning, sub null: a frozen backbone solves later tasks conditioned on retrieved experience. C03 is not assigned under the run convention (r08b AccelOpt): there is no upstream training of a schema parser and no category-level holdout (ALFWorld transfer is seen task types). Supporting reframe_as_solvable_object, sub null, partial: memory selection is recast as a one-step value decision with Monte-Carlo/EMA updates. This is a distinct executed operation (the Q-reranking) that its RE-4 check addresses; the recast is inherited from M-MDP.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C03 not selected: it needs a conditioning schema that a model is trained to parse; the backbone is frozen and only reads retrieved text.
matches.success_checks: Conditioning toggled by controls (No Memory, RAG, lambda=0, single-task retrieval: met); cheaper alternatives (RAG/Self-RAG baselines: met; longer-context baseline: absent); structural/category held-out and contamination analysis (unmet: HLE replays the same questions; ALFWorld held-out are seen task types).
matches.failure_checks: 'True zero-shot / held-out' framing with exposure to the evaluation domain: present for HLE runtime and cross-model claims; baselines receive the same feedback loop (avoided).
matches.reason: The executed operation is solving later tasks by conditioning a frozen model on retrieved prior experience, without parameter updates.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: No sub-card: C21 (RL->supervised relabelling) and C27 (game) do not describe a value-learning recast of retrieval; C00 is interpretability measurement.
matches.success_checks: Retrieval formalised as a Q-value decision (met); correspondence beyond convergence of an EMA under stationarity (unmet; GEM argument is heuristic); faithfulness of Q to causal utility (partial, correlation is circular).
matches.failure_checks: Mechanical re-application of Q-learning to a memory index (partial).
matches.reason: Memory selection is recast as a one-step value-based decision with EMA updates; the recast is inherited from M-MDP.

lambda and Q on/off are separable components (ablated).
